questions.q: What four servers were hardened during this capstone project?
options: Four random servers chosen by Dale
HRU-FILE01 and HRU-APP01 (Windows), and hru-web01 and hru-db01 (Linux)
Every server at Hartwell Regional Utilities
Only the two Linux servers
questions.explain: The project was deliberately scoped in Lesson 1 to a representative handful: two Windows servers and two Linux servers.

questions.q: According to the lesson's skills table, what is the real underlying skill behind Lessons 5-6 (writing and testing the KQL rule), beyond the specific KQL syntax?
options: Memorizing every Sentinel pricing tier
Building and testing a detection before trusting it with real traffic
Disabling unused Windows services
Rotating local administrator passwords
questions.explain: The tool is KQL and Sentinel; the transferable skill is the discipline of testing a detection's logic against known scenarios before relying on it.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say four servers and one detection rule was the RIGHT scope for this project, even though it leaves most of Hartwell's environment untouched?
options: Because Hartwell doesn't have any other servers worth hardening
Because it matched exactly what Dale asked for and proved the baseline and rule work end to end, which is a stronger result than a sprawling, partially-verified effort
Because CIS Benchmarks only support four servers at a time
Because Sentinel limits the number of servers per detection rule
questions.explain: This echoes Lesson 2's point: a small, fully verified scope that matches the actual request is a stronger deliverable than an unfinished attempt at everything.

questions.q: What does this lesson say about the Intermediate tier of Hartwell's security program?
options: It describes the Intermediate tier's exact content in detail
It previews that the program needs to grow well beyond this project, without describing the specific content of that growth
It states there is no further work needed after this project
It recommends skipping straight to an advanced SOC build-out
questions.explain: The wrap-up deliberately sets up, but does not describe, the next tier — that specific content belongs to a separate course.

questions.q: What does the lesson identify as mattering more to a hiring manager than which exact command was typed?
options: The total number of lines of KQL written
The transferable skills underneath the tools — scoping, verification, testing before trusting, documentation, and clear communication under pushback
Whether CIS Level 1 or Level 2 was used
The specific Fish Audio voice used in the course videos
questions.explain: The lesson's skills table makes this explicit: CIS Benchmarks and KQL are the vehicle, while scoping, verification, testing, documentation, and communication are what actually mattered.
